observation.visible_scene: A soft-focus, grayscale view of a pale wall or panel covered with blurred shadows of foliage—palm-like fronds and dense leafy masses—overlaid by a thin dark rectangular grid (window-pane / frame lines) that crosses the image horizontally and vertically. The whole frame is hazy, with no sharp edges.
visible_changes: Over the excerpt the pattern of shadows drifts: the dense dark leafy mass that fills the centre-right in the early frames gradually shifts toward the right, while brighter zones containing more clearly defined palm-frond silhouettes emerge and expand on the left side.
The thin rectangular grid lines translate slightly across the frame (their positions relative to the image edges move a little from the first to the last sampled frame).
The overall soft blur / defocus persists throughout; the leafy shadows appear to sway or change shape subtly rather than one discrete object moving cleanly.
No hard cut is visible; the change reads as continuous slow motion of the shadow pattern and grid.
The relative arrangement of grid lines and shadow blobs stays roughly consistent, so the shift looks like a lateral translation of the scene (or camera) rather than a deformation of the wall itself.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the apparent drift is a camera pan, wind-blown leaves casting moving shadows, or a moving light source is not determinable from this segment.
What lies before frame 1 and after frame 41 (the segment is temporally cropped at both ends).
The true material and identity of the surface and of the rectangular lines (window frame, printed grid, or foreground overlay) are not confirmed.
uncertain_details: Direction and cause of motion (camera movement vs. object/shadow movement) is uncertain; the grid and shadows shift together, which could indicate a pan.
Whether the rectangular lines are on the same plane as the shadows or a separate foreground element is unclear.
The 'palm frond' identification is tentative—only the silhouette shape supports it.
